newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fokker Aviation confirms more Boeing work.
newsitem.headline: Fokker Aviation confirms more Boeing work.

text.p: Aircraft maintenance company Fokker Aviation has won new contracts allowing it to broaden the existing maintenance work it does for Boeing Co, a spokesman for the Dutch company's parent said on Wednesday.

"We already had a licence to do basic maintainance work on Boeing 737s and by this new development that licence has been widened," said Koos Huurdeman, a spokesman for Dutch industrial systems and services group Stork NV.
Stork took over Fokker Aviation, the profitable aircraft maintenance and services arm of bankrupt planemaker Fokker NV, in July.
Fokker Aviation would be involved in more complex work on 737s than the current simple "garage" work it does now, the Stork spokesman said.
"This new agreement means we would go beyond the normal repair work on 737s and do more of the complicated rebuilding jobs -- the full range of repair and maintenance," he said.
"This is our core activity, the more of these sorts of contracts we get, the better," Huurdeman said, adding Fokker Aviation expected to start the new work in the coming weeks.

The agreement at first will cover only a limited number of 737 models although after this breakthrough Stork hopes to work on all five types of 737. The smallest 737 is a competitor for the Fokker 100 regional jet.

Huurdeman declined to comment on how much extra revenue the new work would bring in for Fokker Aviation. "That's information I cannot give because the client does not want that," he said. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
